name: Ambient Clinical Scribes
title: Ambient Clinical Scribes
answer: Ambient clinical scribes are AI systems that capture audio from a patient encounter, usually in an exam room or telehealth visit, and produce a structured clinical note for the clinician's review. They are used across primary care and many specialties to reduce documentation burden, not to make diagnoses or treatment decisions. The output typically includes history of present illness, review of systems, physical exam, assessment, and plan, mapped to the electronic health record. Scope is documentation support, not autonomous care.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Ambient clinical scribes are AI systems that capture audio from a patient encounter, usually in an exam room or telehealth visit, and produce a structured clinical note for the clinician's review. They are used across primary care and many specialties to reduce documentation burden, not to make diagnoses or treatment decisions. The output typically includes history of present illness, review of systems, physical exam, assessment, and plan, mapped to the electronic health record. Scope is documentation support, not autonomous care.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These tools run on cloud speech-to-text and large language model services, with audio captured by a microphone in the room or through the telehealth platform. The audio is streamed or uploaded to a vendor's servers, where it is transcribed and processed. Some deployments use on-device wake words or local encryption before transmission, but the heavy inference generally happens in the cloud. Integration with the EHR is usually through an API or a web application that lets the clinician paste or import the draft note.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work is done in stages. First, automatic speech recognition converts the conversation to text, often with speaker diarization to separate clinician and patient. Then a language model summarizes the transcript into a clinical note, using templates and sometimes specialty-specific prompts. The clinician reviews and edits the draft before signing it in the medical record. The system does not retain the audio by default in many configurations, but the transcript and note may be stored for audit.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on patient consent, data privacy, and accuracy. Patients should be informed when a scribe is listening, and the recording is protected health information under HIPAA in the United States. Risks include hallucinated or omitted clinical details, which is why the clinician must verify every note. Provenance is important: the note should indicate that it was generated with AI assistance and edited by the clinician, so the record reflects human accountability. Some health systems require a notice in the chart or a consent form before use.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Ambient scribes are moving from simple transcription to more structured, coding-aware documentation that can suggest billing codes or flag missing information. Future versions may integrate with clinical decision support, but the core role is likely to remain a drafting assistant under clinician control. Wider adoption depends on reducing error rates, improving support for non-English languages and accents, and building trust through transparent audit trails. The field is also likely to see more specialty-specific templates and tighter EHR integration.
